newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-OLD, NEW FIREBALLERS COMBINE TO BLANK YANKS 1-0.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-OLD, NEW FIREBALLERS COMBINE TO BLANK YANKS 1-0.

text.p: Juan Guzman and Kelvim Escobar combined on a two-hitter and Orlando Merced supplied the offence with a homer off David Cone Friday as the Blue Jays edged the World Series champion New York Yankees 1-0.

Making his second start since returning from a broken thumb, Guzman allowed a leadoff double by Derek Jeter and nothing else in five scoreless innings as he struck out eight and walked one but left a 0-0 game after 74 pitches.
For the second time in six days, 21-year-old rookie Escobar (2-0) relieved Guzman and got the win.
"When I see him, I see myself in '91," Guzman said of Escobar. "He's a good pitcher with great potential."

Escobar (2-0) started the sixth and held the Yanks to one single and one walk over four innings. In his big-league debut last Sunday against division-leading Baltimore, Escobar pitched 4 1-3 innings and gave up just one run.
"Guzman threw a great change," Yankees manager Joe Torre said. "The other guy is like (Yankees ace reliever Mariano) Rivera. That's the kind of stuff he was throwing."

Coming off his worst start of the season, Cone allowed six hits in 7 1/3 innings and struck out seven. He left a sixth-inning fastball up and over the middle of the plate to Merced, who crushed it over wall in right-centre.
"It was a mistake," said Cone (8-4). "That's part of the game. Guzman and Escobar were nasty. I got outpitched."
The shutout temporarily ended New York's dominance at SkyDome, where they had won 13 of their last 16 games.

In Cleveland, Marquis Grissom's two-out, bases-loaded infield single scored Matt Williams with the go-ahead run, capping a three-run eighth inning, as the Cleveland Indians dealt the Kansas City Royals their sixth straight loss 7-6.

Jim Thome led off the eighth with a homer off starter Jose Rosado. Hipolito Pichardo (2-4) relieved and surrendered a single to Manny Ramirez and walks to Williams and Julio Franco around a ground out by Sandy Alomar to load the bases.

Larry Casian entered and allowed a game-tying sacrifice fly to Brian Giles. Omar Vizquel greeted Jeff Montgomery with a single to left reloading the bases for Grissom, whose ground smash was bobbled by second baseman David Howard as Williams scored.
Brian Anderson (3-1) got the win, Mike Jackson the save.
Alomar extended his hitting streak to 29 games with a single in the second inning.

In Chicago, Ozzie Guillen scored the winning run on Heathcliff Slocumb's second wild pitch of the bottom of the ninth inning as the Chicago White Sox edged the Boston Red Sox 6-5 snapping a four-game losing streak.

Guillen opened the ninth with a bouncer up the middle, which he legged to second for a double. He took third on Slocumb's first wild pitch. Ray Durham struck out and Dave Martinez was hit by a pitch before Slocumb was wild again to Darren Lewis, allowing Guillen to race home.
Boston plated three runs in the top of the ninth off reliever Roberto Hernandez to knot the game at 5-5.
At Texas, Lee Stevens capped a five-run third inning with a three-run homer to lead the Texas Rangers to a 7-6 win over the Oakland Athletics.
Stevens, who also had an RBI triple in the second, knocked in four and came within a single of his first career cycle.

"I've never been one hit shy, that's the closest I've ever come. I didn't think about it until after my last at-bat when I realised I only needed a single. At that point, I just wanted to win the game and get it over."
In Detroit, Brian Hunter hit his first grand slam as the Tigers stopped an 11-game losing skid against the Baltimore Orioles with an 11-8 win in the second game of a doubleheader.

Travis Fryman's infield single up the third base line scored Hunter with the run that put Detroit ahead 9-8 in the fourth and relievers Jose Bautista, Doug Brocail and Todd Jones shut the Orioles down the rest of the way.
In the opening game, the Orioles bullpen came through as Arthur Rhodes, Armando Benitez and Randy Myers combined on five innings of shutout relief in Baltimore's 4-3 victory.
Catcher Lenny Webster singled in the go-ahead run for Baltimore in the fifth.
In Seattle, Randy Johnson tossed seven solid innings and Jose Cruz Jr., Edgar Martinez and Paul Sorrento homered to lift the Mariners to a 7-3 win over the Anaheim Angels.
Johnson (12-2) allowed two runs and six hits with four walks and four strikeouts. He improved to 12-5 lifetime against the Angels, beating them for the ninth time in 10 decisions since June 1992.
Cruz and Martinez connected off knuckleballing starter Dennis Springer (4-3), while Sorrento added a solo blast off reliever Shigetoshi Hasegawa.
Tim Salmon and Darin Erstad hit solo homers in the fourth fo Anaheim, losers of eight of their last 10 games.
In Milwaukee, Greg Colbrunn had four hits and four RBI and Terry Steinbach went 4-for-4 as the Minnesota Twins pounded a season-high 23 hits to defeat the Milwaukee Brewers 13-1.
"We had one of those games that everything falls in for you, where all the grounders seem to find the hole," Twins manager Tom Kelly said.
Dave Stevens (1-2) took the win.
"It was just a bad day for the 'Brew Crew,' real bad day all around," Brewers manager Phil Garner said.
